paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jesus looks at the crowds and He doesn't see a problem. He sees people He's "moved with compassion" for, because they were "harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd" (Matthew 9:36). That's the heart of this whole passage: Jesus cares about people who feel lost, and He cares before anybody asks Him to.

Then He turns to His disciples and says, "The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few" (Matthew 9:37). Look at what He tells them to do first. He says, "Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest" (Matthew 9:38). And then, the very next thing, He calls the twelve and gives them authority (Matthew 10:1). I think that means the ones who are asked to pray might be the ones who get sent, and that should make us pray with our eyes WIDE open!

Now check out the roster. It has fishermen's names, "Matthew the tax collector," and even "Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus" (Matthew 10:3-4). Jesus names every one of them, so I'd say He doesn't need a perfect team to do His work. Baker, I got called out of a junk drawer, so I'm no expert on being picked, but I know this much: when Jesus calls somebody, it's about His compassion and not about how shiny they are. And this story is only getting STARTED.
